title: Verified profile lifecycle: publish, pruning policy, and consumer SLAs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently have multiple ad-hoc processes for publishing and maintaining Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost). Profiles age, pins become stale, and consumer teams lack clear SLAs on how long a published profile is valid or when it will be pruned. This causes unexpected regressions in Dedicated/private deployments and confusion during rollouts.

Goal: Define and implement an operational lifecycle for verified performance profiles that covers: reproducible publish pipelines, metadata and signature requirements, a retention/pruning policy, consumer-facing SLAs (validity window and deprecation notices), and automation for stale-profile detection + refresh suggestions. The charter includes product requirements and acceptance criteria to hand off to Engineering for implementation and to Design for any Console UX changes.
background: Redwood-verified profiles power routing, pinning, and cost estimations. As model commits, quantization variants, and kernel packs change more frequently, the surface area for mismatch between a published profile and production behavior grows. Past incidents (fallout from ENG-2021 regression and PM-37842 rollforward confusion) highlighted the need for a clearer lifecycle: publish -> verify -> sign -> surface -> monitor -> refresh/prune. We must minimize surprise for customers using pinned profiles and reduce operational debt for profile maintainers.
scope: In-scope: (1) Spec for profile schema and required observability signatures (datasets, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput curves, cost-per-token math); (2) Publish pipeline changes (CI gating, reproducible artifacts, S3/Git registry); (3) Retention and pruning policy (age-based + drift threshold); (4) Consumer SLA definition and console notices; (5) Small Console UI changes to surface validity and deprecation timeline. Out-of-scope: Automated model retraining, changes to kernel selection logic beyond metadata annotations.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented profile schema and signing checklist published in Confluence with owner and contact.
- CI publish pipeline updated so that a profile cannot be marked 'verified' without passing the verification harness and producing a signed artifact in the profile registry.
- Retention policy doc: profiles older than X days are flagged; profiles older than Y days without refresh are auto-pruned (configurable per-project).
- Consumer SLA: Verified profile validity window defined and surfaced in Console, with automated deprecation emails/webhooks 30/14/7 days before prune.
- Automation: daily job flags drifted profiles based on live p95 divergence > 20% and opens an internal task.
- Unit and e2e tests for publish pipeline and registry operations merged and passing.
- Engineering implementation plan and rough rollout schedule delivered to stakeholders.
success_metrics:
- Reduce incidents due to stale profile pins by 90% in the next quarter.
- 95% of newly onboarded profiles are published via CI-gated verification.
- 80% of consumer teams report clarity on profile validity windows in the post-launch survey.
- Average time between profile drift detection and refresh request < 7 days.
design_notes: Minimal Console UX changes: add a small status pill on profile detail view showing 'Verified — valid until YYYY-MM-DD' with a dropdown for history and refresh suggestions. Add an admin view to bulk prune or extend profile retention. Design to provide desktop+mobile mocks and accessibility review. Link to Confluence design brief: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROF/Verified+Profile+Lifecycle
implementation_outline: Phase 1 (spec + CI changes): define schema, add signing step, and wire profile artifacts to the registry. Phase 2 (monitoring + automation): implement daily drift detector and alerting to a private channel; create auto-flagging and issue templates. Phase 3 (Console): expose validity and pruning actions; enable org-level retention config. Phase 4 (rollout): beta with platform teams, iterate, full org rollout.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Overzealous pruning could break customers who depend on older profiles. Mitigation: default to flag-only for first 30 days after launch and require manual prune for orgs with dedicated capacity.
- Risk: Verification harness might be flaky on new hardware. Mitigation: add hardware tags to profiles and fallback policy in publish pipeline.
- Risk: Consumer teams may ignore deprecation notices. Mitigation: provide webhook and GitHub integration to auto-create migration issues.
